variants.name: 通往新世界
variants.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset: finished English cover for a 16:9 short film about nine creative building projects, "What Can Curiosity Build?". Generate ONE polished full-bleed WIDE 16:9 image, ideally 2048 by 1152 pixels. This is cover design 1: a quiet cinematic invitation into a new world.
Input image 1 is ONLY a subject/material reference for the real project's blue living-water floor and Cosmic Cliffs sky. Input image 2 is ONLY an architectural gallery/sketch reference. Neither is an edit target. Recompose a new cover, not a screenshot montage.
Composition: on the LEFT 47% place a very large, exquisitely spaced warm-ivory editorial serif headline in three lines. On the RIGHT is one striking architectural rectangular museum doorway, seen almost frontally with subtle perspective, resting on a dark matte navy floor. Through its opening we see the luminous cobalt water room with a few water lilies, warm amber Cosmic Cliffs clouds and stars, and a hint of the gallery's painted wall. A little warm-gold chess knight at the threshold is a secondary clue, roughly one tenth of image height. The doorway/frame edges subtly transition from a few pale drafting lines into finished architectural material. One coherent scene, one focal point, generous calm space behind the type.
Text EXACTLY, and nothing else: "What Can" / "Curiosity" / "Build?".
Use large confident Georgia-like serif lettering, clean straight baselines, excellent contrast, headline readable at tiny thumbnail size. Text stays within the left half and safe margins. No small writing.
Mood: thoughtful, welcoming, filled with possibility. Deep midnight navy and restrained ice blue, with one warm amber glow inside the doorway. Elegant lighting and tangible spatial depth, not a generic glowing fantasy portal. A museum film poster rather than a video-game ad.
Avoid: circular sci-fi gates, magical glyphs, excessive bloom, rainbow neon, people, school stock photos, 9-panel collages, browser interface, logos, header/footer, watermarks, labels, extra text, fake formulas, clutter.

variants.name: 从草图到世界
variants.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset: finished English 16:9 video cover for a film showing creative projects moving from an idea through a build process to a working experience. Generate ONE WIDE 16:9 complete cover, ideally 2048 by 1152 pixels. This is design 2: an idea becomes a world.
Input images 1 and 2 are style/subject references ONLY: architectural art-gallery concepts that are half line drawing and half color. Recompose an original cover rather than pasting the images.
Visual concept: on a beautiful warm ivory paper ground, a single large isometric cutaway art gallery evolves across the canvas from delicate graphite/blue construction lines into a richly colored, welcoming three-dimensional painted room. The left part remains unfinished linework; the right becomes the finished environment, with cobalt and gold swirling painted walls, framed artworks and a vivid blue floor. The transition is organic and continuous, not a hard vertical split. The building occupies the lower half and right 65%, with a strong readable architectural silhouette. A few spare curved drafting strokes can suggest the formula-built ride, but no equations, numbers or little annotations.
In the upper LEFT, with generous clear space, place this exact oversized headline, on two lines:
"FROM IDEAS"
"TO WORLDS"
No other text. Choose beautifully balanced dark-navy contemporary editorial serif type, huge enough to dominate a mobile thumbnail. All letters straight, sharp, correctly spelled. Large safe margins. No little captions.
Style: premium illustrated architecture book cover, tactile paper grain, confident fine pencil lines, selective watercolor/gouache, warm and human rather than cold technological blueprints. Deliberately asymmetric composition with generous breathing room. Strong contrast between blank paper, unfinished structure and the finished blue-gold room. Preserve the hand-built curiosity of the film.
Avoid: collage boxes, desktop UI, school icons, people, typography under the illustration, miniature labels, footer, logo, watermark, extra text, dense measurements, generic AI fantasy clutter.

variants.name: 建造、玩耍、探索
variants.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset: complete English video cover for a playful creative-project film with art, math-built rides, chess, puzzles, and coding challenges. Generate ONE full-bleed WIDE 16:9 landscape image, ideally 2048 by 1152 pixels. This is cover design 3: Build, Play, Discover. It must look deliberately different from a quiet portal poster or an architectural paper sketch.
Input image 1 is ONLY a subject/material reference: the real ice-blue formula-built spiral ride, with restrained gold rail edges, floating in space. Rebuild its recognizable continuous spiral geometry with convincing clean construction, not an arbitrary spaghetti roller coaster. Do not copy the screenshot frame or its black letterbox bars.
Composition: very large bold rounded geometric sans-serif typography fills the LEFT 48%, while an oversized tactile warm-gold chess knight sits in the lower RIGHT foreground, confidently occupying about 45% of the image height. Behind it, an ice-blue spiral ride sweeps diagonally up into the upper right and draws the eye through the composition. A subtle cobalt star field and dark blue floor connect the objects as one coherent miniature world. Exactly these two hero subjects; retain bold silhouettes and breathing room. Slight low camera angle, premium stylized 3D materials with soft dimensional lighting; playful and intelligent, no childish clip art.
Headline EXACTLY in three stacked lines, including the periods:
"BUILD."
"PLAY."
"DISCOVER."
Headline must be extremely legible at thumbnail size, cream-white and warm yellow with one restrained ice-blue accent. Nothing overlaps or obscures the letters. Keep wide safe margins. No subtitle or any other text.
Mood: curious, inviting, active. Saturated deep cobalt, clear ice blue, warm golden yellow; not oversaturated candy colors. Clean art direction, controlled contrast, expressive depth without photoreal game clutter. The chess knight and sweeping geometric ride should be immediately recognizable.
Avoid: cubes, people, avatars, faces, controllers, arrows, emojis, fantasy weapons, generic sci-fi portals, excessive glow, tiny writing, labels, logos, watermarks, browser headers, footers, extra text, collage grids.
